- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+15% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak for 2–3 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% per day until reversion completes.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., +0.5+), model often underreacts; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 2–4 days if no major event.  
- If model forecast is consistently >45 and true outcome is <40 for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 2–5% per day).  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near end of period; reduce final 5–7 days by 3–8% if sentiment remains neutral or mildly negative.
